ko.title: 미국 8월 소매판매 1.2% 증가, 그러나 쇼핑객들은 압박감을 느낀다: 지출이 계속될 수 있을까?

segments.src: American shoppers spent more in August than economists expected, even as many of them say their budgets feel tighter than ever.
segments.tr: 많은 미국 쇼핑객들이 예산이 그 어느 때보다 빠듯하다고 말하면서도, 8월에 경제학자들의 예상보다 더 많은 돈을 지출했습니다.

segments.src: Government data show that U.S.
segments.tr: 정부 데이터에 따르면 미국의

segments.src: retail sales rose **1.2% in August to $773.9 billion**.
segments.tr: 소매판매는 **8월에 1.2% 증가한 7,739억 달러**를 기록했습니다.

segments.src: That beat forecasts and was the largest monthly gain since March.
segments.tr: 이는 전망치를 상회한 것이며 지난 3월 이후 가장 큰 월간 상승 폭입니다.

segments.src: On the surface, that is a strong report.
segments.tr: 겉보기에는 강력한 보고서입니다.

segments.src: Look a little deeper, though, and many economists see reasons to be careful.
segments.tr: 하지만 조금 더 깊이 들여다보면, 많은 경제학자들은 주의해야 할 이유를 발견합니다.

segments.src: Gasoline prices are climbing again, wages are not keeping pace with the cost of living, and the Federal Reserve has just raised interest rates.
segments.tr: 휘발유 가격이 다시 오르고 있고, 임금은 생활비를 따라잡지 못하고 있으며, 연방준비제도(Fed)는 방금 금리를 인상했습니다.

segments.src: Together, these forces could weigh on spending in the months ahead.
segments.tr: 이러한 요인들이 결합되어 향후 몇 달 동안 지출에 부담을 줄 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## The Headline Numbers
segments.tr: ## 주요 수치

segments.src: - **Monthly change:** Retail sales increased 1.2% from July.
segments.tr: - **전월 대비 변화:** 소매판매가 7월보다 1.2% 증가했습니다.

segments.src: - **Total sales:** About $773.9 billion for the month.
segments.tr: - **총 매출:** 해당 월에 약 7,739억 달러.

segments.src: - **Versus expectations:** The reading came in above forecasts.
segments.tr: - **예상치 대비:** 수치가 전망치를 상회했습니다.

segments.src: - **Historical context:** It was the biggest one-month gain since March.
segments.tr: - **역사적 맥락:** 지난 3월 이후 가장 큰 단월 상승 폭이었습니다.

segments.src: Retail sales are one of the most closely watched indicators of the U.S.
segments.tr: 소매판매는 미국 경제에서 가장 면밀히 관찰되는 지표 중 하나입니다.

segments.src: economy.
segments.tr: 경제.

segments.src: Consumer spending makes up roughly two-thirds of economic activity, so a strong month at stores, restaurants, gas stations, and online retailers often signals that the broader economy is holding up.
segments.tr: 소비자 지출은 경제 활동의 약 3분의 2를 차지하므로, 상점, 식당, 주유소, 온라인 소매업체의 실적이 좋다는 것은 종종 더 넓은 경제가 잘 버티고 있음을 나타냅니다.

segments.src: ## Why the Boom May Not Last
segments.tr: ## 붐이 지속되지 않을 수 있는 이유

segments.src: ### 1. Pump prices are rising again
segments.tr: ### 1. 주유소 가격이 다시 상승하고 있습니다

segments.src: Retail sales are reported in dollars, not adjusted for price changes.
segments.tr: 소매판매는 가격 변동을 조정하지 않은 달러 금액으로 보고됩니다.

segments.src: That matters because gasoline stations are part of the retail sales total.
segments.tr: 주유소가 소매판매 총액의 일부이기 때문에 이는 중요합니다.

segments.src: When fuel gets more expensive, drivers spend more at the pump, and that spending shows up as a higher retail number even if they are not buying anything extra.
segments.tr: 연료가 더 비싸지면 운전자들은 주유소에서 더 많은 돈을 쓰게 되고, 추가로 구매하는 것이 없더라도 그 지출은 더 높은 소매판매 수치로 나타납니다.

segments.src: In other words, part of a headline gain can reflect higher prices rather than more goods and services.
segments.tr: 즉, 헤드라인 수치의 상승 중 일부는 더 많은 상품과 서비스보다는 더 높은 가격을 반영할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: It also means that money spent on fuel is money that is not available for other purchases.
segments.tr: 또한 연료에 소비된 돈은 다른 구매에 사용할 수 없는 돈임을 의미합니다.

segments.src: If gas prices keep rising, households may need to trim spending elsewhere, such as dining out, clothing, or larger purchases.
segments.tr: 휘발유 가격이 계속 오르면 가계는 외식, 의류 또는 더 큰 규모의 구매 등 다른 곳에서의 지출을 줄여야 할 수도 있습니다.

segments.src: ### 2. Real wages are falling
segments.tr: ### 2. 실질 임금이 하락하고 있습니다

segments.src: "Real" wages are paychecks after accounting for inflation.
segments.tr: "실질" 임금은 인플레이션을 감안한 급여입니다.

segments.src: When prices rise faster than pay, each dollar earned buys less than it did before.
segments.tr: 가격이 급여보다 빠르게 상승하면, 벌어들이는 1달러의 가치는 이전보다 줄어듭니다.

segments.src: Falling real wages tend to erode purchasing power gradually, even when the job market itself looks healthy.
segments.tr: 실질 임금 하락은 고용 시장 자체가 건강해 보일 때도 구매력을 점진적으로 약화시키는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: This is one reason many people say they feel poorer even when their spending totals look strong.
segments.tr: 이것이 많은 사람들이 지출 총액이 튼튼해 보임에도 불구하고 자신이 더 가난해졌다고 느끼는 이유 중 하나입니다.

segments.src: Their paychecks may be larger in dollar terms, but everyday costs such as groceries, rent, insurance, and fuel are taking a bigger share.
segments.tr: 그들의 급여는 달러 기준으로 더 많아졌을지 모르지만, 식료품, 임대료, 보험료, 연료비 같은 일상적인 비용이 더 큰 비중을 차지하고 있습니다.

segments.src: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates
segments.tr: ### 3. 연준이 방금 금리를 인상했습니다

segments.src: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates to cool demand and keep inflation in check.
segments.tr: 연방준비제도는 수요를 식히고 인플레이션을 억제하기 위해 금리를 인상합니다.

segments.src: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can affect credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.
segments.tr: 금리가 높아지면 대출 비용이 더 비싸지며, 이는 신용카드, 자동차 대출, 주택담보대출에 영향을 미칠 수 있습니다.

segments.src: The effects usually arrive with a delay, so a rate increase now may not show up in shopping data right away.
segments.tr: 그 효과는 보통 시차를 두고 나타나므로, 지금의 금리 인상이 쇼핑 데이터에 즉각 나타나지 않을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Over time, though, higher borrowing costs can push consumers to spend more carefully and put off big-ticket purchases.
segments.tr: 그러나 시간이 지남에 따라 높아진 대출 비용은 소비자들이 더 신중하게 지출하고 고가품 구매를 미루도록 만들 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## 압박감을 느끼면서도 지출하는 소비자

segments.src: The August report highlights a familiar puzzle: people say they are worried about prices, yet they keep spending.
segments.tr: 8월 보고서는 익숙한 수수께끼를 강조합니다. 사람들은 물가에 대해 걱정한다고 말하면서도 계속 지출을 하고 있다는 점입니다.

segments.src: There are several possible explanations, and each may play a role for different households:
segments.tr: 여기에는 몇 가지 가능한 설명이 있으며, 가구마다 서로 다른 요인이 작용할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **고용 안정성.** 안정적인 직장을 가진 사람들은 물가에 대해 불안감을 느끼더라도 지출을 계속하는 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **저축 및 신용.** 일부 가구는 생활 방식을 유지하기 위해 저축을 헐거나 신용카드에 더 의존하고 있을 수 있습니다. 이는 당분간 지출을 뒷받침할 수 있지만 영구적인 해결책은 아닙니다.

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **필수 지출.** 필수품 가격이 상승하면 실제 소비 심리가 살아나지 않더라도 지출 총액이 부풀려질 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **시기적 효과.** 특히 일부 구매가 앞당겨진 경우, 한 달 동안의 강력한 실적 뒤에 더 약한 실적이 뒤따를 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: 이러한 요인들 때문에 경제학자들은 일반적으로 한 달 치 데이터에 너무 많은 의미를 부여하지 말라고 경고합니다.

segments.src: Monthly retail figures are often revised, and a strong reading does not guarantee that the trend will continue.
segments.tr: 월간 소매 수치는 종종 수정되며, 강한 수치가 그 추세가 계속될 것임을 보장하지는 않습니다.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## 다음에 주목해야 할 사항

segments.src: If you are following the economy, these are the indicators worth keeping an eye on:
segments.tr: 경제를 주시하고 있다면 다음과 같은 지표들을 눈여겨볼 가치가 있습니다.

segments.src: 1. **Next month's retail sales report.** Does spending hold up, or does August turn out to be an outlier?
segments.tr: 1. **다음 달 소매판매 보고서.** 지출이 유지되는지, 아니면 8월이 일시적인 예외로 드러나는지?

segments.src: 2. **Gasoline prices.** Sustained increases can squeeze budgets and distort spending totals.
segments.tr: 2. **휘발유 가격.** 지속적인 상승은 예산을 압박하고 지출 총액을 왜곡할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: 3. **Inflation and wage data.** The gap between price growth and pay growth shapes how far household budgets can stretch.
segments.tr: 3. **인플레이션 및 임금 데이터.** 물가 상승률과 임금 상승률 사이의 격차는 가계 예산이 얼마나 버틸 수 있는지를 결정합니다.

segments.src: 4. **Consumer sentiment surveys.** These show whether people's stated worries begin to change how they actually spend.
segments.tr: 4. **소비자 심리 조사.** 이는 사람들이 말하는 우려가 실제로 어떻게 소비하는지를 바꾸기 시작하는지 보여줍니다.

segments.src: 5. **Further moves from the Fed.** Additional rate decisions will influence borrowing costs across the economy.
segments.tr: 5. **연준의 추가 행보.** 추가적인 금리 결정은 경제 전반의 대출 비용에 영향을 미칠 것입니다.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 요약

segments.src: August's 1.2% jump shows that American consumers remain a powerful engine of the economy.
segments.tr: 8월의 1.2% 급증은 미국 소비자들이 여전히 경제의 강력한 엔진으로 남아 있음을 보여줍니다.

segments.src: But the strength may be less solid than it appears.
segments.tr: 하지만 그 강세는 보이는 것보다 덜 견고할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Higher fuel costs can inflate the totals, real wages are under pressure, and higher interest rates are likely to make borrowing more costly.
segments.tr: 높아진 연료비가 총액을 부풀릴 수 있고, 실질 임금은 압박을 받고 있으며, 높아진 금리는 대출 비용을 더 비싸게 만들 가능성이 큽니다.

segments.src: Many economists therefore expect spending growth to cool rather than keep accelerating.
segments.tr: 따라서 많은 경제학자들은 지출 증가세가 계속 가속화되기보다는 둔화될 것으로 예상합니다.

segments.src: For households, the practical takeaway is to keep an eye on the budget.
segments.tr: 가계 입장에서 실질적인 시사점은 예산을 계속 주시하는 것입니다.

segments.src: Everyday prices, interest rates on debt, and the difference between "wants" and "needs" all matter more when money feels tight.
segments.tr: 돈이 빠듯하다고 느껴질 때는 일상 물가, 부채 이자율, 그리고 "원하는 것"과 "필요한 것"의 차이가 모두 더 중요해집니다.

segments.src: Economic figures are subject to revision, and forecasts may not prove accurate.
segments.tr: 경제 수치는 수정될 수 있으며, 예측이 정확하지 않을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Why the Boom May Not Last
segments.tr: ## 为什么繁荣可能无法持续

segments.src: ### 1. Pump prices are rising again
segments.tr: ### 1. 油价再次上涨

segments.src: Retail sales are reported in dollars, not adjusted for price changes.
segments.tr: 零售额以美元报告，未针对价格变化进行调整。

segments.src: That matters because gasoline stations are part of the retail sales total.
segments.tr: 这一点很重要，因为加油站是零售总额的一部分。

segments.src: When fuel gets more expensive, drivers spend more at the pump, and that spending shows up as a higher retail number even if they are not buying anything extra.
segments.tr: 当燃料变得更贵时，司机在加油站花费更多，即使他们没有购买任何额外的东西，这种支出也会显示为更高的零售数字。

segments.src: In other words, part of a headline gain can reflect higher prices rather than more goods and services.
segments.tr: 换句话说，头条增长的一部分可能反映了价格上涨，而不是商品和服务数量的增加。

segments.src: It also means that money spent on fuel is money that is not available for other purchases.
segments.tr: 这也意味着花在燃料上的钱是无法用于其他购买的钱。

segments.src: If gas prices keep rising, households may need to trim spending elsewhere, such as dining out, clothing, or larger purchases.
segments.tr: 如果油价持续上涨，家庭可能需要削减其他方面的支出，例如外出就餐、购买服装或进行大额消费。

segments.src: ### 2. Real wages are falling
segments.tr: ### 2. 实际工资正在下降

segments.src: "Real" wages are paychecks after accounting for inflation.
segments.tr: “实际”工资是指扣除通货膨胀后的薪水。

segments.src: When prices rise faster than pay, each dollar earned buys less than it did before.
segments.tr: 当物价上涨速度快于工资增长时，每一美元赚取的收入购买力都比以前低。

segments.src: Falling real wages tend to erode purchasing power gradually, even when the job market itself looks healthy.
segments.tr: 即使在就业市场本身看起来健康的情况下，实际工资下降往往也会逐渐侵蚀购买力。

segments.src: This is one reason many people say they feel poorer even when their spending totals look strong.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么许多人即使在支出总额看起来很强劲时，也感到自己变穷了的原因之一。

segments.src: Their paychecks may be larger in dollar terms, but everyday costs such as groceries, rent, insurance, and fuel are taking a bigger share.
segments.tr: 他们的工资在美元金额上可能更高，但食品杂货、租金、保险和燃料等日常成本占据了更大的份额。

segments.src: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates
segments.tr: ### 3. 美联储刚刚加息

segments.src: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates to cool demand and keep inflation in check.
segments.tr: 美联储提高利率是为了抑制需求并控制通货膨胀。

segments.src: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can affect credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.
segments.tr: 更高的利率使借贷成本变得更昂贵，这会影响信用卡、汽车贷款和抵押贷款。

segments.src: The effects usually arrive with a delay, so a rate increase now may not show up in shopping data right away.
segments.tr: 这种影响通常会有滞后性，因此现在的加息可能不会立即在购物数据中显示出来。

segments.src: Over time, though, higher borrowing costs can push consumers to spend more carefully and put off big-ticket purchases.
segments.tr: 然而，随着时间的推移，更高的借贷成本可能会促使消费者更谨慎地消费，并推迟大额购买。

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## 尽管感到压力但仍在消费的消费者

segments.src: The August report highlights a familiar puzzle: people say they are worried about prices, yet they keep spending.
segments.tr: 8月份的报告突显了一个熟悉的谜题：人们表示担心价格，但他们仍在继续消费。

segments.src: There are several possible explanations, and each may play a role for different households:
segments.tr: 有几种可能的解释，每种解释对不同的家庭可能都起作用：

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **就业稳定性。** 拥有稳定工作的人即使在对价格感到不安时，往往也会继续消费。

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **储蓄和信贷。** 一些家庭可能正在动用储蓄或更多地依赖信贷来维持他们的生活方式。这可以在一段时间内支持消费，但这不是长久之计。

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **必要支出。** 生活必需品价格上涨可能会推高支出总额，而这并不代表真正的信心。

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **时间效应。** 一个强劲的月份之后可能会跟着一个较弱的月份，特别是如果某些购买行为被提前了的话。

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: 由于这些因素，经济学家通常告诫不要过度解读一个月的数据。

segments.src: Monthly retail figures are often revised, and a strong reading does not guarantee that the trend will continue.
segments.tr: 月度零售数据经常会被修正，强劲的读数并不能保证这种趋势会持续下去。

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## 接下来要关注什么

segments.src: If you are following the economy, these are the indicators worth keeping an eye on:
segments.tr: 如果你在关注经济，这些指标值得密切留意：

segments.src: 1. **Next month's retail sales report.** Does spending hold up, or does August turn out to be an outlier?
segments.tr: 1. **下个月的零售销售报告。** 消费能否保持，还是8月只是一个特例？

segments.src: 2. **Gasoline prices.** Sustained increases can squeeze budgets and distort spending totals.
segments.tr: 2. **汽油价格。** 持续上涨可能会挤压预算并扭曲支出总额。

segments.src: 3. **Inflation and wage data.** The gap between price growth and pay growth shapes how far household budgets can stretch.
segments.tr: 3. **通胀和工资数据。** 物价增长与工资增长之间的差距决定了家庭预算的承受能力。

segments.src: 4. **Consumer sentiment surveys.** These show whether people's stated worries begin to change how they actually spend.
segments.tr: 4. **消费者信心调查。** 这些调查显示人们口头上的担忧是否开始改变他们的实际消费方式。

segments.src: 5. **Further moves from the Fed.** Additional rate decisions will influence borrowing costs across the economy.
segments.tr: 5. **美联储的进一步行动。** 额外的利率决策将影响整个经济的借贷成本。

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 总结

segments.src: August's 1.2% jump shows that American consumers remain a powerful engine of the economy.
segments.tr: 8月份1.2%的跃升表明美国消费者仍然是经济的强大引擎。

segments.src: But the strength may be less solid than it appears.
segments.tr: 但这种强劲可能并不像看起来那么稳固。

segments.src: Higher fuel costs can inflate the totals, real wages are under pressure, and higher interest rates are likely to make borrowing more costly.
segments.tr: 更高的燃料成本可能会推高总额，实际工资面临压力，而更高的利率可能会使借贷成本更高。

segments.src: Many economists therefore expect spending growth to cool rather than keep accelerating.
segments.tr: 因此，许多经济学家预计支出增长将会放缓，而不是继续加速。

segments.src: For households, the practical takeaway is to keep an eye on the budget.
segments.tr: 对于家庭而言，实际的启示是密切关注预算。

segments.src: Everyday prices, interest rates on debt, and the difference between "wants" and "needs" all matter more when money feels tight.
segments.tr: 当感到资金紧张时，日常价格、债务利率以及“想要”与“需要”之间的区别都变得更加重要。

segments.src: ## Why the Boom May Not Last
segments.tr: ## Why the Boom May Not Last

segments.src: ### 1. Pump prices are rising again
segments.tr: ### 1. Pump prices are rising again

segments.src: Retail sales are reported in dollars, not adjusted for price changes.
segments.tr: खुदरा बिक्री की रिपोर्ट डॉलर में दी जाती है, कीमत के बदलाव के लिए समायोजित नहीं की जाती।

segments.src: That matters because gasoline stations are part of the retail sales total.
segments.tr: यह मायने रखता है क्योंकि गैस स्टेशन खुदरा बिक्री कुल का हिस्सा हैं।

segments.src: When fuel gets more expensive, drivers spend more at the pump, and that spending shows up as a higher retail number even if they are not buying anything extra.
segments.tr: जब ईंधन अधिक महंगा हो जाता है, तो ड्राइवर पंप पर अधिक खर्च करते हैं, और वह खर्च एक उच्च खुदरा संख्या के रूप में दिखाई देता है, भले ही वे कुछ अतिरिक्त न खरीद रहे हों।

segments.src: In other words, part of a headline gain can reflect higher prices rather than more goods and services.
segments.tr: दूसरे शब्दों में, मुख्य वृद्धि का एक हिस्सा अधिक सामान और सेवाओं के बजाय उच्च कीमतों को दर्शा सकता है।

segments.src: It also means that money spent on fuel is money that is not available for other purchases.
segments.tr: इसका यह भी अर्थ है कि ईंधन पर खर्च किया गया पैसा वह पैसा है जो अन्य खरीदारी के लिए उपलब्ध नहीं है।

segments.src: If gas prices keep rising, households may need to trim spending elsewhere, such as dining out, clothing, or larger purchases.
segments.tr: यदि गैस की कीमतें बढ़ती रहती हैं, तो परिवारों को अन्य जगहों पर खर्च में कटौती करने की आवश्यकता हो सकती है, जैसे कि बाहर खाना, कपड़े पहनना, या बड़ी खरीदारी।

segments.src: ### 2. Real wages are falling
segments.tr: ### 2. Real wages are falling

segments.src: "Real" wages are paychecks after accounting for inflation.
segments.tr: "वास्तविक" मजदूरी मुद्रास्फीति का हिसाब लगाने के बाद वेतन है।

segments.src: When prices rise faster than pay, each dollar earned buys less than it did before.
segments.tr: जब कीमतें वेतन की तुलना में तेजी से बढ़ती हैं, तो अर्जित प्रत्येक डॉलर पहले की तुलना में कम खरीदता है।

segments.src: Falling real wages tend to erode purchasing power gradually, even when the job market itself looks healthy.
segments.tr: गिरती हुई वास्तविक मजदूरी धीरे-धीरे क्रय शक्ति को कम करती है, तब भी जब नौकरी बाजार खुद स्वस्थ दिखता है।

segments.src: This is one reason many people say they feel poorer even when their spending totals look strong.
segments.tr: यह एक कारण है कि कई लोग कहते हैं कि वे गरीब महसूस करते हैं, तब भी जब उनके खर्च के कुल आंकड़े मजबूत दिखते हैं।

segments.src: Their paychecks may be larger in dollar terms, but everyday costs such as groceries, rent, insurance, and fuel are taking a bigger share.
segments.tr: डॉलर के संदर्भ में उनका वेतन बड़ा हो सकता है, लेकिन किराने का सामान, किराया, बीमा और ईंधन जैसी रोजमर्रा की लागतें एक बड़ा हिस्सा ले रही हैं।

segments.src: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates
segments.tr: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates

segments.src: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can affect credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.
segments.tr: उच्च दरों से उधार लेना अधिक महंगा हो जाता है, जो क्रेडिट कार्ड, ऑटो ऋण और बंधक को प्रभावित कर सकता है।

segments.src: The effects usually arrive with a delay, so a rate increase now may not show up in shopping data right away.

segments.src: Over time, though, higher borrowing costs can push consumers to spend more carefully and put off big-ticket purchases.
segments.tr: हालांकि, समय के साथ, उच्च उधार लागत उपभोक्ताओं को अधिक सावधानी से खर्च करने और बड़ी टिकट खरीदारी को टालने के लिए प्रेरित कर सकती है।

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed

segments.tr: अगस्त की रिपोर्ट एक परिचित पहेली को उजागर करती है: लोग कहते हैं कि वे कीमतों के बारे में चिंतित हैं, फिर भी वे खर्च करना जारी रखते हैं।

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **Employment stability.** जिन लोगों के पास स्थिर नौकरियां हैं, वे अक्सर तब भी खर्च करना जारी रखते हैं जब वे कीमतों के बारे में असहज महसूस करते हैं।

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **Savings and credit.** कुछ परिवार अपनी जीवनशैली बनाए रखने के लिए बचत निकाल रहे होंगे या क्रेडिट पर अधिक भरोसा कर रहे होंगे। यह कुछ समय के लिए खर्च का समर्थन कर सकता है, लेकिन यह कोई स्थायी समाधान नहीं है।

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **Necessity spending.** आवश्यक चीजों के लिए उच्च कीमतें वास्तविक विश्वास का संकेत दिए बिना खर्च के कुल को फुला सकती हैं।

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **Timing effects.** एक मजबूत महीने के बाद एक कमजोर महीना आ सकता है, खासकर यदि कुछ खरीदारी को आगे लाया गया हो।

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: इन कारकों के कारण, अर्थशास्त्री आम तौर पर डेटा के एक महीने में बहुत अधिक पढ़ने के खिलाफ चेतावनी देते हैं।

segments.tr: يشكل إنفاق المستهلكين حوالي ثلثي النشاط الاقتصادي، لذا فإن شهراً قوياً في المتاجر والمطاعم ومحطات الوقود وتجار التجزئة عبر الإنترنت غالباً ما يشير إلى أن الاقتصاد الأوسع لا يزال صامداً.

segments.src: ## Why the Boom May Not Last
segments.tr: ## لماذا قد لا يستمر الازدهار

segments.src: ### 1. Pump prices are rising again
segments.tr: ### 1. أسعار الوقود ترتفع مرة أخرى

segments.src: Retail sales are reported in dollars, not adjusted for price changes.
segments.tr: يتم الإبلاغ عن مبيعات التجزئة بالدولار، دون تعديل لتغيرات الأسعار.

segments.src: That matters because gasoline stations are part of the retail sales total.
segments.tr: هذا مهم لأن محطات البنزين جزء من إجمالي مبيعات التجزئة.

segments.src: When fuel gets more expensive, drivers spend more at the pump, and that spending shows up as a higher retail number even if they are not buying anything extra.
segments.tr: عندما يصبح الوقود أكثر تكلفة، ينفق السائقون المزيد في المحطات، ويظهر هذا الإنفاق كرقم تجزئة أعلى حتى لو لم يشتروا أي شيء إضافي.

segments.src: In other words, part of a headline gain can reflect higher prices rather than more goods and services.
segments.tr: بمعنى آخر، يمكن أن يعكس جزء من المكسب الرئيسي ارتفاع الأسعار بدلاً من زيادة السلع والخدمات.

segments.src: It also means that money spent on fuel is money that is not available for other purchases.
segments.tr: يعني هذا أيضاً أن الأموال التي تُنفق على الوقود هي أموال غير متاحة للمشتريات الأخرى.

segments.src: If gas prices keep rising, households may need to trim spending elsewhere, such as dining out, clothing, or larger purchases.
segments.tr: إذا استمرت أسعار البنزين في الارتفاع، فقد تحتاج الأسر إلى تقليص الإنفاق في أماكن أخرى، مثل تناول الطعام في الخارج، أو الملابس، أو المشتريات الكبيرة.

segments.src: ### 2. Real wages are falling
segments.tr: ### 2. الأجور الحقيقية تنخفض

segments.src: "Real" wages are paychecks after accounting for inflation.
segments.tr: الأجور "الحقيقية" هي الرواتب بعد احتساب التضخم.

segments.src: When prices rise faster than pay, each dollar earned buys less than it did before.
segments.tr: عندما ترتفع الأسعار بشكل أسرع من الأجور، فإن كل دولار يتم كسبه يشتري أقل مما كان عليه من قبل.

segments.src: Falling real wages tend to erode purchasing power gradually, even when the job market itself looks healthy.
segments.tr: تميل الأجور الحقيقية المنخفضة إلى تآكل القوة الشرائية تدريجياً، حتى عندما يبدو سوق العمل نفسه صحياً.

segments.src: This is one reason many people say they feel poorer even when their spending totals look strong.
segments.tr: هذا أحد الأسباب التي تجعل الكثير من الناس يقولون إنهم يشعرون بالفقر حتى عندما تبدو إجماليات إنفاقهم قوية.

segments.src: Their paychecks may be larger in dollar terms, but everyday costs such as groceries, rent, insurance, and fuel are taking a bigger share.
segments.tr: قد تكون رواتبهم أكبر من حيث القيمة الدولارية، لكن التكاليف اليومية مثل البقالة والإيجار والتأمين والوقود تأخذ حصة أكبر.

segments.src: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates
segments.tr: ### 3. قام الاحتياطي الفيدرالي للتو برفع أسعار الفائدة

segments.src: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates to cool demand and keep inflation in check.
segments.tr: يرفع الاحتياطي الفيدرالي أسعار الفائدة لتهدئة الطلب وإبقاء التضخم تحت السيطرة.

segments.src: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can affect credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.
segments.tr: تجعل المعدلات الأعلى الاقتراض أكثر تكلفة، مما قد يؤثر على بطاقات الائتمان وقروض السيارات والرهون العقارية.

segments.src: The effects usually arrive with a delay, so a rate increase now may not show up in shopping data right away.
segments.tr: تصل التأثيرات عادةً مع تأخير، لذا قد لا تظهر زيادة أسعار الفائدة الآن في بيانات التسوق على الفور.

segments.src: Over time, though, higher borrowing costs can push consumers to spend more carefully and put off big-ticket purchases.
segments.tr: ومع ذلك، بمرور الوقت، يمكن أن تدفع تكاليف الاقتراض المرتفعة المستهلكين إلى الإنفاق بحذر أكبر وتأجيل المشتريات الكبيرة.

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## مستهلك ينفق رغم شعوره بالضغط

segments.src: The August report highlights a familiar puzzle: people say they are worried about prices, yet they keep spending.
segments.tr: يسلط تقرير أغسطس الضوء على لغز مألوف: يقول الناس إنهم قلقون بشأن الأسعار، ومع ذلك يستمرون في الإنفاق.

segments.src: There are several possible explanations, and each may play a role for different households:
segments.tr: هناك عدة تفسيرات محتملة، وقد يلعب كل منها دوراً بالنسبة للأسر المختلفة:

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **استقرار التوظيف.** غالباً ما يستمر الأشخاص الذين لديهم وظائف ثابتة في الإنفاق حتى عندما يشعرون بعدم الارتياح تجاه الأسعار.

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **المدخرات والائتمان.** قد تقوم بعض الأسر بسحب المدخرات أو الاعتماد بشكل أكبر على الائتمان للحفاظ على نمط حياتهم. يمكن أن يدعم ذلك الإنفاق لفترة من الوقت، لكنه ليس حلاً دائماً.

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **إنفاق الضروريات.** يمكن أن تؤدي الأسعار المرتفعة للأساسيات إلى تضخيم إجماليات الإنفاق دون الإشارة إلى ثقة حقيقية.

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **تأثيرات التوقيت.** يمكن أن يتبع شهراً قوياً واحداً شهر أضعف، خاصة إذا تم تقديم بعض المشتريات.

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: بسبب هذه العوامل، يحذر الاقتصاديون عموماً من المبالغة في قراءة بيانات شهر واحد.

segments.src: Monthly retail figures are often revised, and a strong reading does not guarantee that the trend will continue.
segments.tr: غالباً ما تتم مراجعة أرقام التجزئة الشهرية، والقراءة القوية لا تضمن استمرار الاتجاه.

segments.tr: 1. **تقرير مبيعات التجزئة للشهر المقبل.** هل يستمر الإنفاق، أم أن أغسطس كان مجرد استثناء؟

segments.src: 2. **Gasoline prices.** Sustained increases can squeeze budgets and distort spending totals.

segments.src: 3. **Inflation and wage data.** The gap between price growth and pay growth shapes how far household budgets can stretch.
segments.tr: 3. **بيانات التضخم والأجور.** تشكل الفجوة بين نمو الأسعار ونمو الأجور مدى قدرة ميزانيات الأسرة على الصمود.

segments.src: 5. **Further moves from the Fed.** Additional rate decisions will influence borrowing costs across the economy.
segments.tr: 5. **تحركات إضافية من الاحتياطي الفيدرالي.** ستؤثر قرارات أسعار الفائدة الإضافية على تكاليف الاقتراض في جميع أنحاء الاقتصاد.

segments.tr: Si les prix de l'essence continuent d'augmenter, les ménages devront peut-être réduire leurs dépenses ailleurs, comme les sorties au restaurant, les vêtements ou les achats plus importants.

segments.src: ### 2. Real wages are falling
segments.tr: ### 2. Les salaires réels diminuent

segments.src: "Real" wages are paychecks after accounting for inflation.
segments.tr: Les salaires « réels » sont les salaires après prise en compte de l'inflation.

segments.src: When prices rise faster than pay, each dollar earned buys less than it did before.
segments.tr: Lorsque les prix augmentent plus vite que les salaires, chaque dollar gagné achète moins qu'avant.

segments.src: Falling real wages tend to erode purchasing power gradually, even when the job market itself looks healthy.
segments.tr: La baisse des salaires réels a tendance à éroder progressivement le pouvoir d'achat, même lorsque le marché du travail lui-même semble sain.

segments.src: This is one reason many people say they feel poorer even when their spending totals look strong.
segments.tr: C'est l'une des raisons pour lesquelles de nombreuses personnes disent se sentir plus pauvres même lorsque le total de leurs dépenses semble élevé.

segments.src: Their paychecks may be larger in dollar terms, but everyday costs such as groceries, rent, insurance, and fuel are taking a bigger share.
segments.tr: Leurs salaires sont peut-être plus élevés en termes de dollars, mais les coûts quotidiens tels que l'épicerie, le loyer, l'assurance et le carburant prennent une part plus importante.

segments.src: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates
segments.tr: ### 3. La Fed vient de relever ses taux

segments.src: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates to cool demand and keep inflation in check.
segments.tr: La Réserve fédérale relève les taux d'intérêt pour refroidir la demande et maintenir l'inflation sous contrôle.

segments.src: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can affect credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.
segments.tr: Des taux plus élevés rendent l'emprunt plus cher, ce qui peut affecter les cartes de crédit, les prêts automobiles et les hypothèques.

segments.src: The effects usually arrive with a delay, so a rate increase now may not show up in shopping data right away.
segments.tr: Les effets arrivent généralement avec un décalage, de sorte qu'une hausse des taux maintenant peut ne pas se refléter immédiatement dans les données d'achat.

segments.src: Over time, though, higher borrowing costs can push consumers to spend more carefully and put off big-ticket purchases.
segments.tr: Au fil du temps, cependant, des coûts d'emprunt plus élevés peuvent pousser les consommateurs à dépenser plus prudemment et à reporter leurs achats importants.

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## Un consommateur qui dépense malgré un sentiment de pression

segments.src: The August report highlights a familiar puzzle: people say they are worried about prices, yet they keep spending.
segments.tr: Le rapport d'août met en évidence une énigme familière : les gens disent s'inquiéter des prix, et pourtant ils continuent de dépenser.

segments.src: There are several possible explanations, and each may play a role for different households:
segments.tr: Il existe plusieurs explications possibles, et chacune peut jouer un rôle pour différents ménages :

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **Stabilité de l'emploi.** Les personnes qui ont un emploi stable continuent souvent de dépenser même lorsqu'elles se sentent mal à l'aise face aux prix.

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **Épargne et crédit.** Certains ménages peuvent puiser dans leur épargne ou compter davantage sur le crédit pour maintenir leur mode de vie. Cela peut soutenir les dépenses pendant un certain temps, mais ce n'est pas une solution permanente.

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **Dépenses de première nécessité.** Des prix plus élevés pour les produits essentiels peuvent gonfler le total des dépenses sans signaler une réelle confiance.

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **Effets de calendrier.** Un seul mois fort peut être suivi d'un mois plus faible, en particulier si certains achats ont été anticipés.

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: En raison de ces facteurs, les économistes conseillent généralement de ne pas accorder trop d'importance à un seul mois de données.

segments.src: Monthly retail figures are often revised, and a strong reading does not guarantee that the trend will continue.
segments.tr: Les chiffres mensuels du commerce de détail sont souvent révisés, et une lecture forte ne garantit pas que la tendance se poursuivra.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Ce qu'il faut surveiller ensuite

segments.src: If you are following the economy, these are the indicators worth keeping an eye on:
segments.tr: Si vous suivez l'économie, voici les indicateurs à surveiller :

segments.src: 1. **Next month's retail sales report.** Does spending hold up, or does August turn out to be an outlier?
segments.tr: 1. **Le rapport sur les ventes au détail du mois prochain.** Les dépenses se maintiennent-elles, ou le mois d'août s'avère-t-il être une exception ?

segments.src: 2. **Gasoline prices.** Sustained increases can squeeze budgets and distort spending totals.
segments.tr: 2. **Les prix de l'essence.** Des augmentations soutenues peuvent réduire les budgets et fausser le total des dépenses.

segments.src: 3. **Inflation and wage data.** The gap between price growth and pay growth shapes how far household budgets can stretch.
segments.tr: 3. **Les données sur l'inflation et les salaires.** L'écart entre la hausse des prix et la hausse des salaires détermine la marge de manœuvre des budgets des ménages.

segments.src: 4. **Consumer sentiment surveys.** These show whether people's stated worries begin to change how they actually spend.
segments.tr: 4. **Les enquêtes sur le moral des consommateurs.** Celles-ci montrent si les inquiétudes exprimées par les gens commencent à modifier leur façon de dépenser.

segments.src: 5. **Further moves from the Fed.** Additional rate decisions will influence borrowing costs across the economy.
segments.tr: 5. **D'autres mesures de la Fed.** D'autres décisions sur les taux influenceront les coûts d'emprunt dans toute l'économie.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## L'essentiel

segments.src: August's 1.2% jump shows that American consumers remain a powerful engine of the economy.
segments.tr: Le bond de 1,2 % en août montre que les consommateurs américains restent un moteur puissant de l'économie.

segments.src: But the strength may be less solid than it appears.
segments.tr: Mais la force est peut-être moins solide qu'il n'y paraît.

segments.src: Higher fuel costs can inflate the totals, real wages are under pressure, and higher interest rates are likely to make borrowing more costly.
segments.tr: Des coûts de carburant plus élevés peuvent gonfler les totaux, les salaires réels sont sous pression et des taux d'intérêt plus élevés vont probablement rendre les emprunts plus coûteux.

segments.src: Many economists therefore expect spending growth to cool rather than keep accelerating.
segments.tr: De nombreux économistes s'attendent donc à ce que la croissance des dépenses se tasse plutôt qu'elle ne continue à s'accélérer.

segments.src: For households, the practical takeaway is to keep an eye on the budget.
segments.tr: Pour les ménages, la leçon pratique est de garder un œil sur le budget.

segments.src: Everyday prices, interest rates on debt, and the difference between "wants" and "needs" all matter more when money feels tight.

segments.src: When fuel gets more expensive, drivers spend more at the pump, and that spending shows up as a higher retail number even if they are not buying anything extra.

segments.src: In other words, part of a headline gain can reflect higher prices rather than more goods and services.
segments.tr: Em outras palavras, parte de um ganho principal pode refletir preços mais altos em vez de mais bens e serviços.

segments.tr: Jika harga bensin terus naik, rumah tangga mungkin perlu memangkas pengeluaran di tempat lain, seperti makan di luar, pakaian, atau pembelian yang lebih besar.

segments.src: ### 2. Real wages are falling
segments.tr: ### 2. Upah riil turun

segments.src: "Real" wages are paychecks after accounting for inflation.
segments.tr: Upah "riil" adalah gaji setelah memperhitungkan inflasi.

segments.src: When prices rise faster than pay, each dollar earned buys less than it did before.
segments.tr: Ketika harga naik lebih cepat daripada gaji, setiap dolar yang diperoleh membeli lebih sedikit daripada sebelumnya.

segments.src: Falling real wages tend to erode purchasing power gradually, even when the job market itself looks healthy.
segments.tr: Penurunan upah riil cenderung mengikis daya beli secara bertahap, bahkan ketika pasar kerja itu sendiri terlihat sehat.

segments.src: This is one reason many people say they feel poorer even when their spending totals look strong.
segments.tr: Ini adalah salah satu alasan mengapa banyak orang mengatakan mereka merasa lebih miskin bahkan ketika total pengeluaran mereka terlihat kuat.

segments.src: Their paychecks may be larger in dollar terms, but everyday costs such as groceries, rent, insurance, and fuel are taking a bigger share.
segments.tr: Gaji mereka mungkin lebih besar dalam nilai dolar, tetapi biaya sehari-hari seperti bahan makanan, sewa, asuransi, dan bahan bakar mengambil porsi yang lebih besar.

segments.src: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates
segments.tr: ### 3. The Fed baru saja menaikkan suku bunga

segments.src: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates to cool demand and keep inflation in check.
segments.tr: Federal Reserve menaikkan suku bunga untuk mendinginkan permintaan dan menjaga inflasi tetap terkendali.

segments.src: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can affect credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.
segments.tr: Suku bunga yang lebih tinggi membuat pinjaman menjadi lebih mahal, yang dapat memengaruhi kartu kredit, pinjaman mobil, dan hipotek.

segments.src: The effects usually arrive with a delay, so a rate increase now may not show up in shopping data right away.
segments.tr: Efeknya biasanya datang dengan penundaan, sehingga kenaikan suku bunga sekarang mungkin tidak langsung terlihat dalam data belanja.

segments.src: Over time, though, higher borrowing costs can push consumers to spend more carefully and put off big-ticket purchases.
segments.tr: Namun seiring berjalannya waktu, biaya pinjaman yang lebih tinggi dapat mendorong konsumen untuk berbelanja dengan lebih hati-hati dan menunda pembelian barang-barang besar.

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## Konsumen yang Tetap Berbelanja Meskipun Merasa Tertekan

segments.src: The August report highlights a familiar puzzle: people say they are worried about prices, yet they keep spending.
segments.tr: Laporan bulan Agustus menyoroti teka-teki yang sudah tidak asing lagi: orang-orang mengatakan mereka khawatir tentang harga, namun mereka tetap berbelanja.

segments.src: There are several possible explanations, and each may play a role for different households:
segments.tr: Ada beberapa penjelasan yang mungkin, dan masing-masing mungkin memainkan peran untuk rumah tangga yang berbeda:

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **Stabilitas pekerjaan.** Orang yang memiliki pekerjaan tetap sering kali terus berbelanja bahkan ketika mereka merasa tidak nyaman dengan harga-harga.

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **Tabungan dan kredit.** Beberapa rumah tangga mungkin menarik tabungan atau lebih mengandalkan kredit untuk mempertahankan gaya hidup mereka. Hal itu dapat mendukung pengeluaran untuk sementara waktu, tetapi itu bukan solusi permanen.

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **Pengeluaran kebutuhan.** Harga yang lebih tinggi untuk barang-barang penting dapat menggelembungkan total pengeluaran tanpa menandakan kepercayaan diri yang nyata.

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **Efek waktu.** Satu bulan yang kuat dapat diikuti oleh bulan yang lebih lemah, terutama jika beberapa pembelian ditarik ke depan.

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: Karena faktor-faktor ini, para ekonom umumnya memperingatkan agar tidak terlalu banyak membaca data satu bulan saja.

segments.src: Monthly retail figures are often revised, and a strong reading does not guarantee that the trend will continue.
segments.tr: Angka ritel bulanan sering kali direvisi, dan angka yang kuat tidak menjamin bahwa tren tersebut akan berlanjut.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Apa yang Harus Diperhatikan Selanjutnya

segments.src: If you are following the economy, these are the indicators worth keeping an eye on:
segments.tr: Jika Anda mengikuti perkembangan ekonomi, ini adalah indikator-indikator yang layak untuk terus diawasi:

segments.src: 1. **Next month's retail sales report.** Does spending hold up, or does August turn out to be an outlier?
segments.tr: 1. **Laporan penjualan ritel bulan depan.** Apakah pengeluaran tetap bertahan, atau apakah bulan Agustus ternyata merupakan anomali?

segments.src: 2. **Gasoline prices.** Sustained increases can squeeze budgets and distort spending totals.
segments.tr: 2. **Harga bensin.** Kenaikan yang berkelanjutan dapat menekan anggaran dan mendistorsi total pengeluaran.

segments.src: 3. **Inflation and wage data.** The gap between price growth and pay growth shapes how far household budgets can stretch.
segments.tr: 3. **Data inflasi dan upah.** Kesenjangan antara pertumbuhan harga dan pertumbuhan gaji menentukan seberapa jauh anggaran rumah tangga dapat diregangkan.

segments.src: 4. **Consumer sentiment surveys.** These show whether people's stated worries begin to change how they actually spend.
segments.tr: 4. **Survei sentimen konsumen.** Ini menunjukkan apakah kekhawatiran yang dinyatakan orang-orang mulai mengubah cara mereka berbelanja yang sebenarnya.

segments.src: 5. **Further moves from the Fed.** Additional rate decisions will influence borrowing costs across the economy.
segments.tr: 5. **Langkah lebih lanjut dari The Fed.** Keputusan suku bunga tambahan akan memengaruhi biaya pinjaman di seluruh perekonomian.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Kesimpulan

segments.src: August's 1.2% jump shows that American consumers remain a powerful engine of the economy.
segments.tr: Lonjakan 1,2% di bulan Agustus menunjukkan bahwa konsumen Amerika tetap menjadi mesin perekonomian yang kuat.

segments.src: But the strength may be less solid than it appears.
segments.tr: Namun kekuatan tersebut mungkin kurang solid dari yang terlihat.

segments.src: Higher fuel costs can inflate the totals, real wages are under pressure, and higher interest rates are likely to make borrowing more costly.
segments.tr: Biaya bahan bakar yang lebih tinggi dapat menggelembungkan total pengeluaran, upah riil berada di bawah tekanan, dan suku bunga yang lebih tinggi kemungkinan akan membuat pinjaman menjadi lebih mahal.

segments.src: Many economists therefore expect spending growth to cool rather than keep accelerating.
segments.tr: Oleh karena itu, banyak ekonom memperkirakan pertumbuhan pengeluaran akan mendingin daripada terus meningkat.

segments.src: For households, the practical takeaway is to keep an eye on the budget.
segments.tr: Bagi rumah tangga, pelajaran praktisnya adalah untuk terus mengawasi anggaran.

segments.src: Everyday prices, interest rates on debt, and the difference between "wants" and "needs" all matter more when money feels tight.
segments.tr: Harga kebutuhan sehari-hari, suku bunga utang, dan perbedaan antara "keinginan" dan "kebutuhan" semuanya menjadi lebih penting ketika uang terasa ketat.

ja.title: 米8月小売売上高は1.2%増、しかし消費者は家計の圧迫を実感：この支出は維持できるか？

segments.src: American shoppers spent more in August than economists expected, even as many of them say their budgets feel tighter than ever.
segments.tr: 米国の消費者は、多くの人がかつてないほど家計が苦しいと感じていると答えているにもかかわらず、8月にはエコノミストの予想を上回る支出を行いました。

segments.src: Government data show that U.S.
segments.tr: 政府のデータによると、米国の

segments.src: retail sales rose **1.2% in August to $773.9 billion**.
segments.tr: 小売売上高は8月に**1.2%増の7,739億ドル**に達しました。

segments.src: That beat forecasts and was the largest monthly gain since March.
segments.tr: これは予測を上回り、3月以来で最大の月次増加幅となりました。

segments.src: On the surface, that is a strong report.
segments.tr: 表面上は、これは力強い報告です。

segments.src: Look a little deeper, though, and many economists see reasons to be careful.
segments.tr: しかし、もう少し深く見てみると、多くのエコノミストは注意すべき理由があると考えています。

segments.src: Gasoline prices are climbing again, wages are not keeping pace with the cost of living, and the Federal Reserve has just raised interest rates.
segments.tr: ガソリン価格が再び上昇しており、賃金は生活費の上昇に追いついておらず、連邦準備制度（FRB）は金利を引き上げたばかりです。

segments.src: Together, these forces could weigh on spending in the months ahead.
segments.tr: これらの要因が重なり、今後数ヶ月の支出を圧迫する可能性があります。

segments.src: ## The Headline Numbers
segments.tr: ## 主要な数値

segments.src: - **Monthly change:** Retail sales increased 1.2% from July.
segments.tr: - **前月比：** 小売売上高は7月から1.2%増加しました。

segments.src: - **Total sales:** About $773.9 billion for the month.
segments.tr: - **総売上高：** 同月は約7,739億ドル。

segments.src: - **Versus expectations:** The reading came in above forecasts.
segments.tr: - **予想との比較：** 予測を上回る結果となりました。

segments.src: - **Historical context:** It was the biggest one-month gain since March.
segments.tr: - **歴史的背景：** 3月以来で最大の単月増加幅となりました。

segments.src: Retail sales are one of the most closely watched indicators of the U.S.
segments.tr: 小売売上高は、米国経済において最も注視されている指標の一つです。

segments.src: economy.
segments.tr: 経済活動。

segments.src: Consumer spending makes up roughly two-thirds of economic activity, so a strong month at stores, restaurants, gas stations, and online retailers often signals that the broader economy is holding up.
segments.tr: 個人消費は経済活動の約3分の2を占めているため、店舗、レストラン、ガソリンスタンド、オンライン小売業者での好調な月は、広範な経済が持ちこたえていることを示すシグナルとなることがよくあります。

segments.src: ## Why the Boom May Not Last
segments.tr: ## なぜこのブームが長続きしない可能性があるのか

segments.src: ### 1. Pump prices are rising again
segments.tr: ### 1. ガソリン価格が再び上昇している

segments.src: Retail sales are reported in dollars, not adjusted for price changes.
segments.tr: 小売売上高はドル建てで報告され、価格変動の調整は行われません。

segments.src: That matters because gasoline stations are part of the retail sales total.
segments.tr: ガソリンスタンドが小売売上高の合計に含まれているため、これは重要です。

segments.src: When fuel gets more expensive, drivers spend more at the pump, and that spending shows up as a higher retail number even if they are not buying anything extra.
segments.tr: 燃料が高くなると、ドライバーはガソリンスタンドでの支出を増やし、その支出は、追加で何も購入していなくても、小売売上高の増加として現れます。

segments.src: In other words, part of a headline gain can reflect higher prices rather than more goods and services.
segments.tr: 言い換えれば、見出しの増加の一部は、商品やサービスの増加ではなく、価格の上昇を反映している可能性があります。

segments.src: It also means that money spent on fuel is money that is not available for other purchases.
segments.tr: また、燃料に費やされたお金は、他の購入に回せないお金であることを意味します。

segments.src: If gas prices keep rising, households may need to trim spending elsewhere, such as dining out, clothing, or larger purchases.
segments.tr: ガソリン価格が上昇し続ければ、世帯は外食、衣料品、あるいはより高額な購入など、他の場所での支出を削る必要があるかもしれません。

segments.src: ### 2. Real wages are falling
segments.tr: ### 2. 実質賃金が低下している

segments.src: "Real" wages are paychecks after accounting for inflation.
segments.tr: 「実質」賃金とは、インフレを考慮した後の給与のことです。

segments.src: When prices rise faster than pay, each dollar earned buys less than it did before.
segments.tr: 給与よりも物価の上昇が早い場合、稼いだ1ドルの価値は以前よりも低下します。

segments.src: Falling real wages tend to erode purchasing power gradually, even when the job market itself looks healthy.
segments.tr: 実質賃金の低下は、雇用市場自体が健全に見える場合でも、購買力を徐々に蝕む傾向があります。

segments.src: This is one reason many people say they feel poorer even when their spending totals look strong.
segments.tr: これが、支出総額が好調に見えるにもかかわらず、多くの人が貧しくなったと感じると言う理由の一つです。

segments.src: Their paychecks may be larger in dollar terms, but everyday costs such as groceries, rent, insurance, and fuel are taking a bigger share.
segments.tr: ドル建てでの給与は増えているかもしれませんが、食料品、家賃、保険、燃料などの日常的なコストがより大きな割合を占めるようになっています。

segments.src: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates
segments.tr: ### 3. FRBが金利を引き上げたばかりである

segments.src: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates to cool demand and keep inflation in check.
segments.tr: 連邦準備制度（FRB）は、需要を冷やし、インフレを抑制するために金利を引き上げます。

segments.src: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can affect credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.
segments.tr: 金利の上昇は借入コストを高くし、クレジットカード、自動車ローン、住宅ローンに影響を与える可能性があります。

segments.src: The effects usually arrive with a delay, so a rate increase now may not show up in shopping data right away.
segments.tr: その効果は通常、遅れて現れるため、現時点での利上げがすぐに買い物データに現れるとは限りません。

segments.src: Over time, though, higher borrowing costs can push consumers to spend more carefully and put off big-ticket purchases.
segments.tr: しかし、時間が経つにつれて、借入コストの上昇は消費者に慎重な支出を促し、高額商品の購入を先送りさせることになります。

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## 家計の圧迫を感じながらも支出する消費者

segments.src: The August report highlights a familiar puzzle: people say they are worried about prices, yet they keep spending.
segments.tr: 8月の報告は、よく知られた謎を浮き彫りにしています。人々は物価を心配していると言いながらも、支出を続けているのです。

segments.src: There are several possible explanations, and each may play a role for different households:
segments.tr: これにはいくつかの考えられる説明があり、世帯によってそれぞれ異なる役割を果たしている可能性があります。

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **雇用の安定。** 安定した仕事を持っている人は、物価に不安を感じていても支出を続けることがよくあります。

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **貯蓄とクレジット。** 一部の世帯は、生活水準を維持するために貯蓄を取り崩したり、クレジットカードへの依存度を高めたりしている可能性があります。これは一時的に支出を支えることができますが、永続的な解決策ではありません。

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **必要不可欠な支出。** 必需品の価格上昇は、実際の自信を示すことなく、支出総額を押し上げる可能性があります。

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **タイミングの影響。** 特に一部の購入が前倒しされた場合、1ヶ月の好調な月の後に弱い月が続くことがあります。

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: これらの要因があるため、エコノミストは一般的に、1ヶ月分のデータのみを過大に解釈しないよう警告しています。

segments.src: Monthly retail figures are often revised, and a strong reading does not guarantee that the trend will continue.
segments.tr: 月次の小売数値は頻繁に改定され、好調な数値がそのトレンドの継続を保証するものではありません。

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## 次に注目すべきこと

segments.tr: 経済を追っている場合、以下の指標に注目する価値があります。

segments.src: 4. **Consumer sentiment surveys.** These show whether people's stated worries begin to change how they actually spend.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 結論

segments.src: August's 1.2% jump shows that American consumers remain a powerful engine of the economy.

segments.src: But the strength may be less solid than it appears.
segments.tr: しかし、その強さは見かけほど強固ではないかもしれません。

segments.tr: そのため、多くのエコノミストは、支出の伸びが加速し続けるのではなく、減速すると予想しています。

segments.src: ## Why the Boom May Not Last
segments.tr: ## Warum der Boom nicht von Dauer sein muss

segments.src: ### 1. Pump prices are rising again
segments.tr: ### 1. Die Preise an den Zapfsäulen steigen wieder

segments.src: Retail sales are reported in dollars, not adjusted for price changes.
segments.tr: Einzelhandelsumsätze werden in Dollar ausgewiesen und sind nicht um Preisänderungen bereinigt.

segments.src: That matters because gasoline stations are part of the retail sales total.
segments.tr: Das ist wichtig, weil Tankstellen Teil der gesamten Einzelhandelsumsätze sind.

segments.src: When fuel gets more expensive, drivers spend more at the pump, and that spending shows up as a higher retail number even if they are not buying anything extra.
segments.tr: Wenn Kraftstoff teurer wird, geben Autofahrer mehr an der Zapfsäule aus, und diese Ausgaben schlagen sich in einer höheren Einzelhandelszahl nieder, selbst wenn sie nichts zusätzlich kaufen.

segments.src: In other words, part of a headline gain can reflect higher prices rather than more goods and services.
segments.tr: Mit anderen Worten: Ein Teil des Zuwachses in den Schlagzeilen kann eher höhere Preise als mehr Waren und Dienstleistungen widerspiegeln.

segments.src: It also means that money spent on fuel is money that is not available for other purchases.
segments.tr: Es bedeutet auch, dass Geld, das für Kraftstoff ausgegeben wird, für andere Einkäufe nicht zur Verfügung steht.

segments.src: If gas prices keep rising, households may need to trim spending elsewhere, such as dining out, clothing, or larger purchases.
segments.tr: Wenn die Benzinpreise weiter steigen, müssen die Haushalte ihre Ausgaben möglicherweise an anderer Stelle einschränken, etwa bei Restaurantbesuchen, Kleidung oder größeren Anschaffungen.

segments.src: ### 2. Real wages are falling
segments.tr: ### 2. Die Reallöhne sinken

segments.src: "Real" wages are paychecks after accounting for inflation.
segments.tr: „Real“-Löhne sind die Gehaltsabrechnungen nach Berücksichtigung der Inflation.

segments.src: When prices rise faster than pay, each dollar earned buys less than it did before.
segments.tr: Wenn die Preise schneller steigen als die Löhne, kauft jeder verdiente Dollar weniger als zuvor.

segments.src: Falling real wages tend to erode purchasing power gradually, even when the job market itself looks healthy.
segments.tr: Sinkende Reallöhne neigen dazu, die Kaufkraft allmählich zu untergraben, selbst wenn der Arbeitsmarkt selbst gesund aussieht.

segments.src: This is one reason many people say they feel poorer even when their spending totals look strong.
segments.tr: Dies ist ein Grund, warum viele Menschen angeben, sich ärmer zu fühlen, selbst wenn ihre Gesamtausgaben hoch aussehen.

segments.src: Their paychecks may be larger in dollar terms, but everyday costs such as groceries, rent, insurance, and fuel are taking a bigger share.
segments.tr: Ihre Gehaltszettel mögen in Dollar ausgedrückt größer sein, aber die alltäglichen Kosten wie Lebensmittel, Miete, Versicherungen und Kraftstoff nehmen einen größeren Anteil ein.

segments.src: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates
segments.tr: ### 3. Die Fed hat gerade die Zinsen angehoben

segments.src: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates to cool demand and keep inflation in check.
segments.tr: Die Federal Reserve erhöht die Zinssätze, um die Nachfrage abzukühlen und die Inflation in Schach zu halten.

segments.src: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can affect credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.
segments.tr: Höhere Zinsen machen die Kreditaufnahme teurer, was sich auf Kreditkarten, Autokredite und Hypotheken auswirken kann.

segments.src: The effects usually arrive with a delay, so a rate increase now may not show up in shopping data right away.
segments.tr: Die Auswirkungen treten in der Regel mit einer Verzögerung ein, sodass sich eine Zinserhöhung jetzt möglicherweise nicht sofort in den Einkaufsdaten niederschlägt.

segments.src: Over time, though, higher borrowing costs can push consumers to spend more carefully and put off big-ticket purchases.
segments.tr: Im Laufe der Zeit können höhere Kreditkosten die Verbraucher jedoch dazu veranlassen, vorsichtiger zu wirtschaften und größere Anschaffungen aufzuschieben.

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## Ein Verbraucher, der trotz gefühlter Enge Geld ausgibt

segments.src: The August report highlights a familiar puzzle: people say they are worried about prices, yet they keep spending.
segments.tr: Der August-Bericht hebt ein bekanntes Rätsel hervor: Die Menschen sagen, sie seien besorgt über die Preise, geben aber dennoch weiterhin Geld aus.

segments.src: There are several possible explanations, and each may play a role for different households:
segments.tr: Dafür gibt es mehrere mögliche Erklärungen, und jede kann bei verschiedenen Haushalten eine Rolle spielen:

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **Beschäftigungsstabilität.** Menschen mit sicheren Arbeitsplätzen geben oft auch dann weiterhin Geld aus, wenn sie sich wegen der Preise unwohl fühlen.

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **Ersparnisse und Kredite.** Einige Haushalte greifen möglicherweise auf Ersparnisse zurück oder verlassen sich mehr auf Kredite, um ihren Lebensstil aufrechtzuerhalten. Das kann die Ausgaben eine Zeit lang stützen, ist aber keine dauerhafte Lösung.

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **Notwendige Ausgaben.** Höhere Preise für lebensnotwendige Güter können die Gesamtausgaben in die Höhe treiben, ohne echtes Vertrauen zu signalisieren.

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **Timing-Effekte.** Auf einen einzelnen starken Monat kann ein schwächerer folgen, insbesondere wenn einige Käufe vorgezogen wurden.

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: Aufgrund dieser Faktoren warnen Ökonomen im Allgemeinen davor, zu viel in die Daten eines einzelnen Monats hineinzuinterpretieren.

segments.src: Monthly retail figures are often revised, and a strong reading does not guarantee that the trend will continue.
segments.tr: Monatliche Einzelhandelszahlen werden häufig revidiert, und ein starker Wert ist keine Garantie dafür, dass sich der Trend fortsetzt.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Was als Nächstes zu beachten ist

segments.src: If you are following the economy, these are the indicators worth keeping an eye on:
segments.tr: Wenn Sie die Wirtschaft verfolgen, sind dies die Indikatoren, die Sie im Auge behalten sollten:

segments.src: 1. **Next month's retail sales report.** Does spending hold up, or does August turn out to be an outlier?
segments.tr: 1. **Der Einzelhandelsumsatzbericht des nächsten Monats.** Halten die Ausgaben an oder erweist sich der August als Ausreißer?

segments.src: 2. **Gasoline prices.** Sustained increases can squeeze budgets and distort spending totals.
segments.tr: 2. **Benzinpreise.** Anhaltende Steigerungen können die Budgets belasten und die Gesamtausgaben verzerren.

segments.src: 3. **Inflation and wage data.** The gap between price growth and pay growth shapes how far household budgets can stretch.
segments.tr: 3. **Inflations- und Lohndaten.** Die Kluft zwischen Preiswachstum und Lohnwachstum bestimmt, wie weit die Haushaltsbudgets gedehnt werden können.

segments.src: 4. **Consumer sentiment surveys.** These show whether people's stated worries begin to change how they actually spend.
segments.tr: 4. **Umfragen zur Verbraucherstimmung.** Diese zeigen, ob die geäußerten Sorgen der Menschen beginnen, ihr tatsächliches Konsumverhalten zu verändern.

segments.src: 5. **Further moves from the Fed.** Additional rate decisions will influence borrowing costs across the economy.
segments.tr: 5. **Weitere Schritte der Fed.** Zusätzliche Zinsentscheidungen werden die Kreditkosten in der gesamten Wirtschaft beeinflussen.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Das Fazit

segments.src: August's 1.2% jump shows that American consumers remain a powerful engine of the economy.
segments.tr: Der Sprung von 1,2 % im August zeigt, dass die amerikanischen Verbraucher weiterhin ein starker Motor der Wirtschaft sind.

segments.src: But the strength may be less solid than it appears.
segments.tr: Doch die Stärke ist möglicherweise weniger solide, als es den Anschein hat.

segments.src: Higher fuel costs can inflate the totals, real wages are under pressure, and higher interest rates are likely to make borrowing more costly.
segments.tr: Höhere Kraftstoffkosten können die Gesamtsummen aufblähen, die Reallöhne stehen unter Druck und höhere Zinssätze dürften die Kreditaufnahme verteuern.

segments.src: Many economists therefore expect spending growth to cool rather than keep accelerating.
segments.tr: Viele Ökonomen erwarten daher eher eine Abkühlung des Ausgabenwachstums als eine weitere Beschleunigung.

segments.src: For households, the practical takeaway is to keep an eye on the budget.
segments.tr: Für die Haushalte lautet die praktische Erkenntnis, das Budget im Auge zu behalten.

segments.src: Everyday prices, interest rates on debt, and the difference between "wants" and "needs" all matter more when money feels tight.
segments.tr: Alltägliche Preise, Zinssätze für Schulden und der Unterschied zwischen „Wünschen“ und „Bedürfnissen“ spielen alle eine größere Rolle, wenn das Geld knapp wird.

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## Người tiêu dùng vẫn chi tiêu mặc dù cảm thấy áp lực

segments.src: The August report highlights a familiar puzzle: people say they are worried about prices, yet they keep spending.
segments.tr: Báo cáo tháng 8 làm nổi bật một câu hỏi quen thuộc: mọi người nói họ lo lắng về giá cả, nhưng họ vẫn tiếp tục chi tiêu.

segments.src: There are several possible explanations, and each may play a role for different households:
segments.tr: Có một số lời giải thích khả thi, và mỗi lời giải thích có thể đóng một vai trò đối với các hộ gia đình khác nhau:

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **Sự ổn định việc làm.** Những người có công việc ổn định thường tiếp tục chi tiêu ngay cả khi họ cảm thấy bất an về giá cả.

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **Tiết kiệm và tín dụng.** Một số hộ gia đình có thể đang rút tiền tiết kiệm hoặc dựa nhiều hơn vào tín dụng để duy trì lối sống của họ. Điều đó có thể hỗ trợ chi tiêu trong một thời gian, nhưng đó không phải là giải pháp vĩnh viễn.

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **Chi tiêu thiết yếu.** Giá cao hơn cho các nhu yếu phẩm có thể làm tăng tổng chi tiêu mà không báo hiệu sự tự tin thực sự.

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **Hiệu ứng thời gian.** Một tháng mạnh mẽ đơn lẻ có thể tiếp theo là một tháng yếu hơn, đặc biệt nếu một số giao dịch mua sắm được kéo lên trước.

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: Do những yếu tố này, các nhà kinh tế nhìn chung cảnh báo không nên đọc quá nhiều vào dữ liệu của một tháng.

segments.src: Monthly retail figures are often revised, and a strong reading does not guarantee that the trend will continue.
segments.tr: Số liệu bán lẻ hàng tháng thường được sửa đổi, và một kết quả cao không đảm bảo rằng xu hướng sẽ tiếp tục.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Cần theo dõi những gì tiếp theo

segments.src: If you are following the economy, these are the indicators worth keeping an eye on:
segments.tr: Nếu bạn đang theo dõi nền kinh tế, đây là những chỉ số đáng chú ý:

segments.src: 1. **Next month's retail sales report.** Does spending hold up, or does August turn out to be an outlier?
segments.tr: 1. **Báo cáo doanh số bán lẻ của tháng tới.** Chi tiêu có giữ vững không, hay tháng 8 hóa ra lại là một ngoại lệ?

es.title: Las ventas minoristas en EE. UU. aumentaron un 1.2% en agosto, pero los compradores sienten la presión: ¿podrá mantenerse el gasto?

segments.src: American shoppers spent more in August than economists expected, even as many of them say their budgets feel tighter than ever.
segments.tr: Los compradores estadounidenses gastaron más en agosto de lo que esperaban los economistas, incluso cuando muchos de ellos dicen que sus presupuestos se sienten más ajustados que nunca.

segments.src: Government data show that U.S.
segments.tr: Los datos del gobierno muestran que en EE. UU.

segments.src: retail sales rose **1.2% in August to $773.9 billion**.
segments.tr: las ventas minoristas aumentaron un **1.2% en agosto a $773.9 mil millones**.

segments.src: That beat forecasts and was the largest monthly gain since March.
segments.tr: Eso superó los pronósticos y fue el mayor aumento mensual desde marzo.

segments.src: On the surface, that is a strong report.
segments.tr: En la superficie, ese es un informe sólido.

segments.src: Look a little deeper, though, and many economists see reasons to be careful.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, si se analiza un poco más a fondo, muchos economistas ven razones para ser cautelosos.

segments.src: Gasoline prices are climbing again, wages are not keeping pace with the cost of living, and the Federal Reserve has just raised interest rates.
segments.tr: Los precios de la gasolina están subiendo de nuevo, los salarios no siguen el ritmo del costo de vida y la Reserva Federal acaba de aumentar las tasas de interés.

segments.src: Together, these forces could weigh on spending in the months ahead.
segments.tr: Juntas, estas fuerzas podrían afectar el gasto en los próximos meses.

segments.src: ## The Headline Numbers
segments.tr: ## Las cifras principales

segments.src: - **Monthly change:** Retail sales increased 1.2% from July.
segments.tr: - **Cambio mensual:** Las ventas minoristas aumentaron un 1.2% desde julio.

segments.src: - **Total sales:** About $773.9 billion for the month.
segments.tr: - **Ventas totales:** Aproximadamente $773.9 mil millones para el mes.

segments.src: - **Versus expectations:** The reading came in above forecasts.
segments.tr: - **Frente a las expectativas:** La lectura se situó por encima de los pronósticos.

segments.src: - **Historical context:** It was the biggest one-month gain since March.
segments.tr: - **Contexto histórico:** Fue el mayor aumento en un mes desde marzo.

segments.src: Retail sales are one of the most closely watched indicators of the U.S.
segments.tr: Las ventas minoristas son uno de los indicadores más observados de la economía de EE. UU.

segments.src: economy.
segments.tr: economía.

segments.src: Consumer spending makes up roughly two-thirds of economic activity, so a strong month at stores, restaurants, gas stations, and online retailers often signals that the broader economy is holding up.
segments.tr: El gasto del consumidor representa aproximadamente dos tercios de la actividad económica, por lo que un mes fuerte en tiendas, restaurantes, gasolineras y minoristas en línea a menudo indica que la economía en general se mantiene firme.

segments.src: ## Why the Boom May Not Last
segments.tr: ## Por qué el auge puede no durar

segments.src: ### 1. Pump prices are rising again
segments.tr: ### 1. Los precios en las gasolineras están subiendo de nuevo

segments.src: Retail sales are reported in dollars, not adjusted for price changes.
segments.tr: Las ventas minoristas se reportan en dólares, sin ajustar por los cambios de precios.

segments.src: That matters because gasoline stations are part of the retail sales total.
segments.tr: Eso importa porque las estaciones de gasolina son parte del total de ventas minoristas.

segments.src: When fuel gets more expensive, drivers spend more at the pump, and that spending shows up as a higher retail number even if they are not buying anything extra.
segments.tr: Cuando el combustible se vuelve más caro, los conductores gastan más en la gasolinera, y ese gasto aparece como una cifra minorista más alta incluso si no están comprando nada extra.

segments.src: In other words, part of a headline gain can reflect higher prices rather than more goods and services.
segments.tr: En otras palabras, parte de un aumento en los titulares puede reflejar precios más altos en lugar de más bienes y servicios.

segments.src: It also means that money spent on fuel is money that is not available for other purchases.
segments.tr: También significa que el dinero gastado en combustible es dinero que no está disponible para otras compras.

segments.src: If gas prices keep rising, households may need to trim spending elsewhere, such as dining out, clothing, or larger purchases.
segments.tr: Si los precios de la gasolina siguen subiendo, los hogares pueden necesitar recortar gastos en otros lugares, como salir a comer, ropa o compras más grandes.

segments.src: ### 2. Real wages are falling
segments.tr: ### 2. Los salarios reales están cayendo

segments.src: "Real" wages are paychecks after accounting for inflation.
segments.tr: Los salarios "reales" son los cheques de pago después de contabilizar la inflación.

segments.src: When prices rise faster than pay, each dollar earned buys less than it did before.
segments.tr: Cuando los precios suben más rápido que los salarios, cada dólar ganado compra menos de lo que compraba antes.

segments.src: Falling real wages tend to erode purchasing power gradually, even when the job market itself looks healthy.
segments.tr: La caída de los salarios reales tiende a erosionar el poder adquisitivo gradualmente, incluso cuando el mercado laboral en sí parece saludable.

segments.src: This is one reason many people say they feel poorer even when their spending totals look strong.
segments.tr: Esta es una razón por la que muchas personas dicen que se sienten más pobres incluso cuando sus totales de gasto parecen sólidos.

segments.src: Their paychecks may be larger in dollar terms, but everyday costs such as groceries, rent, insurance, and fuel are taking a bigger share.
segments.tr: Sus cheques de pago pueden ser más grandes en términos de dólares, pero los costos diarios como comestibles, alquiler, seguros y combustible están ocupando una mayor parte.

segments.src: ### 3. The Fed has just raised rates
segments.tr: ### 3. La Fed acaba de aumentar las tasas

segments.src: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates to cool demand and keep inflation in check.
segments.tr: La Reserva Federal aumenta las tasas de interés para enfriar la demanda y mantener la inflación bajo control.

segments.src: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can affect credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.
segments.tr: Las tasas más altas hacen que el endeudamiento sea más costoso, lo que puede afectar las tarjetas de crédito, los préstamos para automóviles y las hipotecas.

segments.src: The effects usually arrive with a delay, so a rate increase now may not show up in shopping data right away.
segments.tr: Los efectos generalmente llegan con un retraso, por lo que un aumento de tasas ahora puede no aparecer en los datos de compras de inmediato.

segments.src: Over time, though, higher borrowing costs can push consumers to spend more carefully and put off big-ticket purchases.
segments.tr: Con el tiempo, sin embargo, los costos de endeudamiento más altos pueden empujar a los consumidores a gastar con más cuidado y posponer las compras importantes.

segments.src: ## A Consumer Who Spends Despite Feeling Squeezed
segments.tr: ## Un consumidor que gasta a pesar de sentirse presionado

segments.src: The August report highlights a familiar puzzle: people say they are worried about prices, yet they keep spending.
segments.tr: El informe de agosto destaca un rompecabezas familiar: la gente dice que está preocupada por los precios, pero sigue gastando.

segments.src: There are several possible explanations, and each may play a role for different households:
segments.tr: Hay varias explicaciones posibles, y cada una puede desempeñar un papel para diferentes hogares:

segments.src: - **Employment stability.** People who have steady jobs often keep spending even when they feel uneasy about prices.
segments.tr: - **Estabilidad laboral.** Las personas que tienen trabajos estables a menudo siguen gastando incluso cuando se sienten inquietas por los precios.

segments.src: - **Savings and credit.** Some households may be drawing down savings or relying more on credit to maintain their lifestyle. That can support spending for a while, but it is not a permanent solution.
segments.tr: - **Ahorros y crédito.** Algunos hogares pueden estar reduciendo sus ahorros o dependiendo más del crédito para mantener su estilo de vida. Eso puede respaldar el gasto por un tiempo, pero no es una solución permanente.

segments.src: - **Necessity spending.** Higher prices for essentials can inflate spending totals without signaling real confidence.
segments.tr: - **Gasto en necesidades.** Los precios más altos de los artículos esenciales pueden inflar los totales de gasto sin señalar una confianza real.

segments.src: - **Timing effects.** A single strong month can be followed by a weaker one, particularly if some purchases were pulled forward.
segments.tr: - **Efectos de tiempo.** Un solo mes fuerte puede ser seguido por uno más débil, particularmente si algunas compras se adelantaron.

segments.src: Because of these factors, economists generally caution against reading too much into one month of data.
segments.tr: Debido a estos factores, los economistas generalmente advierten contra dar demasiada importancia a un mes de datos.

segments.src: Monthly retail figures are often revised, and a strong reading does not guarantee that the trend will continue.
segments.tr: Las cifras minoristas mensuales a menudo se revisan, y una lectura fuerte no garantiza que la tendencia continuará.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Qué observar a continuación

segments.src: If you are following the economy, these are the indicators worth keeping an eye on:
segments.tr: Si está siguiendo la economía, estos son los indicadores que vale la pena vigilar:

segments.src: 1. **Next month's retail sales report.** Does spending hold up, or does August turn out to be an outlier?
segments.tr: 1. **El informe de ventas minoristas del próximo mes.** ¿Se mantiene el gasto o agosto resulta ser una anomalía?

segments.src: 2. **Gasoline prices.** Sustained increases can squeeze budgets and distort spending totals.
segments.tr: 2. **Precios de la gasolina.** Los aumentos sostenidos pueden presionar los presupuestos y distorsionar los totales de gasto.

segments.src: 3. **Inflation and wage data.** The gap between price growth and pay growth shapes how far household budgets can stretch.
segments.tr: 3. **Datos de inflación y salarios.** La brecha entre el crecimiento de los precios y el crecimiento de los salarios determina hasta dónde pueden llegar los presupuestos de los hogares.

segments.src: 4. **Consumer sentiment surveys.** These show whether people's stated worries begin to change how they actually spend.
segments.tr: 4. **Encuestas de sentimiento del consumidor.** Estas muestran si las preocupaciones declaradas de las personas comienzan a cambiar cómo gastan realmente.

segments.src: 5. **Further moves from the Fed.** Additional rate decisions will influence borrowing costs across the economy.
segments.tr: 5. **Más movimientos de la Fed.** Las decisiones adicionales sobre las tasas influirán en los costos de endeudamiento en toda la economía.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## La conclusión

segments.src: August's 1.2% jump shows that American consumers remain a powerful engine of the economy.
segments.tr: El salto del 1.2% de agosto muestra que los consumidores estadounidenses siguen siendo un motor poderoso de la economía.

segments.src: But the strength may be less solid than it appears.
segments.tr: Pero la fortaleza puede ser menos sólida de lo que parece.

segments.src: Higher fuel costs can inflate the totals, real wages are under pressure, and higher interest rates are likely to make borrowing more costly.
segments.tr: Los costos más altos del combustible pueden inflar los totales, los salarios reales están bajo presión y es probable que las tasas de interés más altas hagan que el endeudamiento sea más costoso.

segments.src: Many economists therefore expect spending growth to cool rather than keep accelerating.
segments.tr: Por lo tanto, muchos economistas esperan que el crecimiento del gasto se enfríe en lugar de seguir acelerándose.

segments.src: For households, the practical takeaway is to keep an eye on the budget.
segments.tr: Para los hogares, la conclusión práctica es vigilar el presupuesto.
